## Line 445 (missing stop in the pinned source)

Not edited here, as instructed. The line as pinned ends "ἀΰσας" with no mark. 413 is the same line with the name changed, and the source prints "ἀΰσας·" there; both introduce a speech that begins on the next line. An ano teleia (·) at the end of 445 is therefore plausible as the edition’s own punctuation (same formula, same position, a speech follows), and it fits the unit as drafted (unit 445 ends with a colon in `l`/`i`, as 413 does). Orchestrator to apply README rule 5 and add the mark to the source, re-pin, and fix `t` of that unit.

## Findings considered and refused

- **"wore" for φορέεσκε of the breastplate (372, 398) beside "carried" of the shield (407).** The drafter’s departure is recorded in new-renderings.md. Refused as a defect: published iliad-062 (440) ships "to wear" for φορέειν of armour, and both `l` keep "kept carrying". The two nouns differ, and "wore a shield" would be wrong.
- **"deem" (`l`) / "reckon" (`i`) for ἐΐσκομεν (446) against the table’s "liken".** Table 5.181 and 13.313 are the transitive "compare"; here ἐΐσκω takes the infinitive ("we think it is worth …"). Departure is stated in new-renderings.md and in the note. Kept.
- **ἔνδον ἐόντα (363) rendered "inside the city" in `i`.** Alternative: say nothing and keep "within". Kept because the context ("out of Troy", 367) supports it and the note says plainly that the Greek does not; cost of the alternative is a dangling "within".
- **`l` of 381 "follow me"** (no pronoun in ἕπε’). Natural English object; the note gives ἕπεο. Not worth a change.
- **"ἀχερωΐς … white poplar" and "βλωθρή … tall" committed in the translation** with "usually taken" in the note. Consistent with how the house treats uncertain epithets (table rows for ἀργεϊφόντης etc.). Kept.
- **Treating 376’s θυγατέρα lengthening as only "metrical lengthening"** (i.e. no note). Refused: the published parts (2.492 in iliad-012, Odyssey 19.400) record this very licence in the note.
- **Changing `i` "called his orders to the Danaans" (361).** Slightly stiff but accurate for κελεύσας; no better rendering found without importing remembered English.
- **Moving "Antilochus, son of great-hearted Nestor" / "steadfast in the fray"** from new-renderings to the table now: not the reviewer’s job (the publisher copies the rows).
- **Possible `i` repetition "wise-hearted as he was" (418)** — table pattern, kept.

## Pass 2 — gloss.json

Coverage: all 103 novel forms have an entry, none extra. All entries under 230 characters, typographic ’ only, no line numbers, no "here". The 12 `__broaden__` entries were compared with `iliad-glossary.json`: each is the old entry whole + " · " + the new reading, and each new reading is true of its line (δρῦς nom. sg. 389; δίφρου after πρόσθ’ 392; εἰς + gen. 415; εὐξαμένοιο gen. abs. 417; ἀσπίδι after ὑπό 405; ἔσχετο with ὑπό in tmesis 368; ἅλιον "in vain" 410; τῇ … ὕπο 408; ὕπο + dat.; ἑταίρου 419; ἠέ 425; βροτῶν 374).

| form · field | sev | what was wrong | what done |
|---|---|---|---|
| πέφνε, πεφάσθαι | M | Lemma θείνω; the glossary already files ἔπεφνε, ἔπεφν’, πεφνέμεν under φένω, and my note on 363 says φένω. Two lemmata for one root. | Both now "φένω (aor. ἔπεφνον) — …"; πεφάσθαι parsed as perf. inf. pass. |
| δουπῆσαι | M | "fall with a crash": units now say "thud" (pass 1). | "fall with a thud". |
| ἐάλη | L | "epic root aorist": it is the second aorist passive of εἴλω. | "aor. 3 sg. pass. (ἐάλη, from the root ϝαλ-)". |
| ἐκπέρσῃς | L | "short-vowel subj." is false; ἐκπέρσῃς is an ordinary 2 sg. aor. subj. | Removed; "with κε". |
| συνώμεθα | M | Flagged doubt; parse stated as certain. | Marked "the usual explanation of συνώμεθα", as in the note at 381. |

Doubts the glosser flagged: ἐεδνωταί ("traditional sense", from ἕεδνα) and καβησόθεν (lemma Κάβησος, suffix -θεν; "site not known") are honest as written; ὄρινεν ("impf. (or aor.)", unaugmented) is correct, since the unaugmented form cannot tell the two apart. All three kept.

Refused: pinned-looking glosses ("agreeing with a fem. noun such as κόνιος", "of the knees" under ἔλυσε) — they name no line and the existing glossary uses such contexts; "Ἄσιος, son of Hyrtacus" (not in this part, but true of the name). ἔλυσε "ὑπό in tmesis": ὑπολύω is the normal reading; kept.
